messages.author: daffc1958e88638f
messages.subject: sumstats: all scheduled cores encountered errors in user code
parts:
Dear all,
An error occurred during the "prepare the sumstats for gwas" conducted on a HPC cluster as below:
Error in UseMethod("tbl_vars") :
no applicable method for 'tbl_vars' applied to an object of class "try-error"
In addition: Warning message:
In mclapply(X = 1:length, FUN = function(X) { :
all scheduled cores encountered errors in user code
Execution halted

The followring arguments used in the sumstats function:
sumstats(files=files, ref=ref, trait.names=trait.names, se.logit=se.logit, OLS=NULL, linprob=NULL, prop=prop, N=N, info.filter=0.6, maf.filter=0.01, keep.indel=FALSE, parallel=TRUE, cores=4)

There are 19 files involved. The error occurred after preparing the first 14 files. I thought this might be caused by the 14th or 15th file, so I conducted sumstats() on either one of them, no issue was raised; however, when working on the two of them, the same issue was replicated.

Does anyone have a clue of what might cause the above error?

Many thanks,
patrick

I meant log files were generated for the first 14 traits when I said after preparing for 14 files. Please find the full scripts below for arguments.

p_sumstats <- sumstats(files=files, ref=ref, trait.names=trait.names, se.logit=se.logit, OLS=NULL, linprob=NULL, prop=prop, N=N, info.filter=info.filter, maf.filter=maf.filter, keep.indel=keep.indel, parallel=parallel, cores=cores)

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: sumstats: all scheduled cores encountered errors in user code
parts:
Hi Patrick, 

Glad you found the issue! The package should have printed some kind of warning to the respective .log files for those traits, but it sounds like that didn't happen? I will have to look into that.

One thing I wanted to bring up is that for your OLS and se.logit arguments you have some cases where both are set to TRUE, which shouldn't be the case as OLS reflects a GWAS for a continuous outcome and se.logit is to indicate that there were logistic standard errors from a case/control GWAS. I would just double check that piece before moving forward. If any of that doesn't make sense let us know!

-Andrew
